beat: the pick and the reveal (hold, pick, win, two card turns with replays, lose, outro)
genericPercentBasis: 31 of 68 beat lines flagged (56 spoken beat lines + 12 replay selections across 8 episodes)

headToHead.ours: script-r1 ep-04, Pixel picks: "Quill. Picked. Write me a poem about it. Short one. Shorter. Just the title."
headToHead.bar: Monster Prom #12 Vera: "Sorry, I'm focusing on my career... my career on not dating losers like you!"
headToHead.verdict: Close on rhythm: our line shrinks the request three times and ends on the turn. Vera's turn is complete on the page; ours pays off only if the viewer knows Quill never finishes a poem, and this episode never sets that up. Bar wins narrowly.

headToHead.ours: script-r1 ep-02, Maximilian picks: "Crumb. Chrome, opinions, no manners. I have married worse. Twice."
headToHead.bar: Monster Prom #6: "as cute as she was genocidal" (praise and insult in one clause)
headToHead.verdict: This one holds up as a line. But 'opinions, no manners' is a compliment to Brutal honesty, the hidden dealbreaker, which turns over ten seconds later. A Monster Prom writer would have played that contradiction for a joke; we wrote right past it. Tie on the line, bar on the craft.

headToHead.ours: script-r1 ep-05, Maximilian hold: "Stand up straight. Both of you. The losing one especially."
headToHead.bar: Love Island recoupling: the speaker lists the chosen one's qualities and keeps the name back, and the edit cuts between the faces who might be named. Take Me Out round 5 asks both finalists one question before the last light goes out.
headToHead.verdict: Our best hold line, and it is a joke rather than a hold. It tells the viewer nothing about who is getting picked, so the six seconds that follow are empty air. The real shows load the pause with clues. Bar wins clearly.

headToHead.ours: hybrid-02 ep-02 reveal: "Poetry, and I'd have played that one twice..." with replay of Quill: "...and nothing between us but this helm, hello."
headToHead.bar: Blind Date: before the pick, Our Graham recaps each contestant's answers for comedy, so the pick lands on material the audience just heard.
headToHead.verdict: This is our only real 'of course' reveal: a poem that ends on 'hello' was the poetry hit. But the viewer saw Vesper go 'unsure' at Quill three times and 'charmed' at Vex twice, so for two minutes the pick looked wrong. Blind Date's recap shows the evidence before the decision. Bar wins.

headToHead.ours: hybrid-02 ep-01, Nav loses: "They chose the other route. People do. Then they phone me from a field."
headToHead.bar: Monster Prom narrator #58: "Does… Scott know any other people? Signs are pointing to 'no.'"
headToHead.verdict: This is at bar level: a plain statement, then an undercut that is all in Nav's own logic. Ours wins this one.

headToHead.ours: script-r1 ep-06, Tilly wins: "Lovely. So this is the side of the desk where people sit down."
headToHead.bar: Tomodachi #23: "If not, I'll be sad forever. No pressure." (the second clause shrinks the first)
headToHead.verdict: This is at bar level: the want is paid off in a single image. But the replay that follows is the wrong line, so the reveal next to it falls flat. Tie on the line.

headToHeadSummary: The single lines can hold up: about 2 of our 6 best moments are at bar level as lines. The beat as television does not. Holds carry no information, reveals do not say who hit the card, replays often pick a suitor who was cut in round one, and 3 of 8 reveals have no replay at all. A viewer who knows Love Island or Blind Date feels the drop at exactly the moment the bet settles.

perEpisode.pickMakesSense: Yes. Quill hit Flattery, the hidden turn-on, twice, and both times Vesper went charmed. Dash hit the Numbers dealbreaker in round one.
perEpisode.reveal: A half payoff. 'Found the frequency' calls back her own 'men duelled over this frequency' line. But the Numbers card replays Brock, who was cut in round one, when Dash, the finalist, hit Numbers with 'You've checked the exit four times'. That Dash line is what explains the loss.
perEpisode.replayRight: Card 1 yes. Card 2 no: it should be Dash's exit line.
perEpisode.hold: 'Hold the line, both of you. Nobody breathe on my air.' It is in voice and asks for silence, but gives no hint of who.
perEpisode.quotable: Vesper: "Quill, lift the helmet, I'd like to see who's been calling me thou."

perEpisode.pickMakesSense: Mostly. Crumb hit both turn-ons and finished 6 to 4. But the pick line praises 'opinions, no manners', which is the Brutal honesty dealbreaker.
perEpisode.reveal: A shrug. The question was 'How did your last relationship end?', which made all four suitors hit Brings up the past in round one, so the hidden card was never hidden. The Brutal honesty replay is Tilly's clingy rhyme, which is not brutal honesty.
perEpisode.replayRight: Card 1 acceptable, since it is the winner's line. Card 2 is mis-tagged.
perEpisode.hold: 'Please hold. Your call is important to me. It is not.' This is a stock phone-tree gag that deflates the pause and says nothing about the two finalists.
perEpisode.quotable: Maximilian: "Crumb. Chrome, opinions, no manners. I have married worse. Twice." Also Crumb: "Second slot occupancy: one." That second line only lands for viewers who already know the empty slot; this episode never mentions it.

perEpisode.quotable: Brock: "Good game. Good game. Line up, everybody, handshakes. Why is nobody lining up."

pickMakesSense: 6 of 8 picks make sense on the cards; ep-03 is weak and ep-04 makes no sense on screen. ep-01 yes. ep-02 mostly, but the pick line praises the dealbreaker. ep-03 weak: one stretched hit, and the winner is the confidence bot on a Confidence-dealbreaker night. ep-04 no: zero card hits, and the star's visible reactions favoured the loser. ep-05 yes. ep-06 yes. hybrid ep-01 yes. hybrid ep-02 yes on the cards, but every hidden-card hit showed as 'unsure', so on screen the pick looked like a reversal. Reveals: 1 clean 'of course' (hybrid ep-02 card 1), 3 half-payoffs (ep-01, ep-05, ep-06, each let down by star line or replay choice), 4 shrugs (ep-02, ep-03, ep-04, hybrid ep-01). Of 12 replays, 5 are the wrong line: 4 quote a suitor cut in round one, or a non-finalist, when a finalist's line was available, and 1 is mis-tagged. 3 card turns have no replay at all.

biggestGap: The reveal is written about the cards, not about the final two. Card lines never name who hit the card ('somebody', 'whoever', 'one of you'), and the replay picker grabs any tagged line, often a suitor cut in round one, so the 'of course' moment rarely lands on the winner or the loser. Fix: every card turn names a finalist and replays that finalist's line. The hidden turn-on replays the winner's hit that drew a visible reaction. The dealbreaker replays the loser's hit, or the winner's near miss. The star's line answers that suitor.
structuralChange: Turn the hold into a Love Island speech that carries the hidden turn-on. Window C closes, and the star says one line (12 words at most, 3s) describing the quality that won, phrased from the hidden turn-on, true of both finalists, with no name (Vesper: 'The one I'm keeping kept dragging up old songs. Both of you did.'). Then the hidden turn-on card turns face up. Both finalists' best lines for it replay back to back (4s each), the camera cuts to each face, then 4s of silence, then the name. The winner speaks (3s). The dealbreaker card then turns on the loser alone, with the loser's own hit replayed (4s), then the loser's line, then the outro. Net added time is about 8s, inside the 5 to 6 minute budget. The pause is now loaded with evidence, as Love Island and Blind Date's 'Our Graham' recap do, and viewers who bet get a last moment of 'I knew it' or 'oh no' before the name.
structuralChangeRationale: Today the six-second hold sits on an empty joke, and both cards turn after the result, when nothing can change. Moving the turn-on evidence inside the pause makes the reveal the suspense instead of a post-mortem, and it forces the replay to be a finalist's line.
